content:
Mike C: quick follow-up from the migration RFC — I want to sketch a hybrid path: keep local token-buckets at each frontdoor shard for fast admission, and run small raft groups to reconcile and rebalance long-lived credits. thinking about correctness/latency tradeoffs.
Elaine: sounds promising. main risk i see is state thrash when many tenants burst across shards — raft chatter + frequent reallocs could spike p99.
Sara: agree on thrash. can we keep reconcile slow (eg 5-30s) and do emergency pulls only when local bucket < X? combine with soft-shed for shortfalls.
Tom: what's the failure model? if raft leaders partition, do we risk double-spend? how to enforce global caps?
Mike C: design thought: local buckets are authoritative for short windows (millis→secs). raft reconciles ownership for longer windows. global caps enforced by raft consensus periodically; in partition we fall back to conservative local caps that are a subset of known global commitment.
Elaine: fallback conservative caps is safe but will degrade throughput. metrics we need: reconcile messaging qps, p99 admission latency, frequency of emergency pulls, and percent of requests shed due to conservative fallback.
Sara: abuse integration question — should abuse score be applied at local admission or only during raft reconciliation? if local ignores abuse then bad actors can farm many shards.
Mike C: proposal: apply a light-weight local abuse heuristic (fast signals) for immediate admission, and a heavier ML abuse score fed asynchronously by the abuse pipeline. heavier scores can trigger raft-driven global penalties and rebalances.
Tom: so local flow: token-bucket check -> fast_abuse_check (rule-based) -> admit. async path: ML_score arrives -> if high, mark tenant for global penalize -> raft triggers credit steal or longer-term eviction.
Sara: that split seems reasonable. need to ensure score feedback loop is closed quickly enough to matter (not hours). maybe aim for 30-120s reaction.
Mike C: config sketch:
```
admission:
  local_mode: true
  local_bucket_size_tokens: 1000
  emergency_threshold_pct: 15
  reconcile_interval_ms: 5000
  raft_group_size: 5
  abuse_integration: "fast_local_rules + async_ml"
```
Elaine: nit: make reconcile_interval tunable per-tenant class. high-tier customers get more frequent reconciliation (lower eventual deviation) and better SLA. low-tier use longer windows.
Tom: operationally we should capture these failure modes in the chaos tests: leader partitions, full network split between two raft groups, and sudden tenant spike across 50% of shards.
Mike C: agreed. I'll add a perf harness that can simulate 10k tenants with mixed burst patterns and run across our staging racks.
rls-bot: deploy-checker: new perf-harness branch exists: refs/heads/hybrid-tokenbucket-proto. CI: perf tests queued.
Sara: telemetry hooks: prefer keeping per-tenant time-series of local_remaining_tokens, reconcile_delta, last_ml_score_timestamp, and admission_reason_counter (local_allow, local_deny, global_override).
Elaine: also emit raft_reassign_events and rebalancing_latency to catch thrash loops.
Tom: one more tradeoff: complexity vs ops burden. raft groups add operational surface (leader elections, data dir management). we should prototype using our existing raft infra component to reduce new code.
Mike C: good point — reuse existing raft infra. initial rollout plan:
- Phase 0: keep central quota service, add local token-bucket shim (no raft) for fast-path, metricize.
- Phase 1: enable raft-backed reconciliation in read-only mode (observe rebalance suggestions but do not enforce).
- Phase 2: switch to raft authoritative for reconciles and enable emergency pulls.
- Phase 3: tighten abuse feedback loop and per-tenant tuning.
Sara: timeline?
Mike C: prototype + perf harness in 2 weeks, internal RFC with details next week, small canary in staging in ~6 weeks if perf looks good.
Elaine: I'll own telemetry PR. Tom can you draft chaos scenarios?
Tom: on it, will post scenarios tomorrow.
Mike C: awesome. action items: Mike -> write up prototype RFC and perf plan; Elaine -> telemetry PR; Tom -> chaos scenarios; Sara -> abuse feedback latency SLA. :thumbsup:
Elaine: :thumbsup:
Sara: :shipit:
Tom: :thinking: if we see too much thrash we should have a feature-flag to roll back to central-only mode quickly.
Mike C: made note of rollback-flag. thanks all — will push the prototype branch and RFC link once ready.
